newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sixth Russia beet test 15.2 pct sugar content.
newsitem.headline: Sixth Russia beet test 15.2 pct sugar content.

text.p: Russia's sixth sugar beet test showed an average sugar content of 15.2 percent compared to 15.1 percent in 1995, the head of the Rossakhsvyokla sugar beet producers' association said on Monday.
Mikhail Sushkov provided the following data for the September 10 test, which the association added to its original testing schedule-
"We still expect the beet harvest to total 17 million tonnes," Sushkov said.
He predicted 1996 yields would be 16.0 tonnes per hectare, down from 17.5 tonnes in 1995.
"This year was dry and so the harvest will be lower," he said.
He said harvesting had begun and about 50,000 tonnes of sugar beets had been gathered but the pace of the harvest had been slow due to wet weather.
"It rained all last week and the harvest stopped, but the rain has already ended and the harvest will begin again," he said.
Last year's sugar beet output was officially 19.1 million tonnes.
Sushkov said a seventh, additional test had been conducted and that results would be available mid-week.
